claims.claim: UK house prices rose 0.5 percent in the year to October according to Nationwide, the slowest pace in more than two years, with the average price at £273,566.
claims.episode_span: Nationwide reported UK house prices rose just 0.5 percent in the year to October, the weakest pace since 2024. The average price stood at £273,566, unchanged from the previous month and down from 0.8 percent in the year to September.
claims.source_title: UK house prices grow at slowest pace in two years as mortgage rates rise
claims.supporting_quote: UK house prices grew by an annual rate of just 0.5% in October, the slowest pace in more than two years, as higher mortgage rates put off potential buyers. The average price for a property in the UK stood at £273,566 in October, flat on the previous month and down from 0.8% in the year to September, according to the lender Nationwide.

claims.claim: Eight companies submitted applications for Hong Kong ride-hailing licences before Friday’s deadline under the new regulatory regime.
claims.episode_span: The Transport Department confirmed that eight companies, including Uber, Didi Chuxing and Singapore-based Tada, submitted applications before the deadline for operating ride-hailing services.
claims.source_title: 8 companies apply for Hong Kong ride-hailing licences ahead of deadline
claims.supporting_quote: Eight companies have applied for licences to provide ride-hailing services in Hong Kong under the new regulatory regime ahead of Friday’s deadline, the Transport Department has confirmed.

claims.claim: Governor Nabil Shamsan of Taiz said Houthi forces have cut oxygen, food and water supplies during a month-long siege, with rubbish piling up and massacres reported.
claims.episode_span: The governor of Taiz said Houthi forces have cut oxygen, food and water supplies during a month-long siege of Yemen’s third-largest city. Rubbish is piling up and massacres are reported.
claims.source_title: Houthis sending Taiz ‘back to the stone age’, governor of besieged Yemen city says
claims.supporting_quote: Nabil Shamsan said massacres were taking place in Yemen’s third city, that oxygen and water supplies were running out and that rubbish was piling up in the streets due to landfill sites being either full or inaccessible.
